items.title: Kimi released giant open multimodal weights
items.oneliner: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro with 2.8T parameters and 1M context, raising the floor for open multimodal agents.

items.title: Ripple pushed open coding benchmarks higher
items.oneliner: Ripple-65B claims 80.52 on agentic coding after 12T tokens and $32M, making open-weight coding models harder to dismiss.

items.title: Anthropic made verifiable inference more practical
items.oneliner: Anthropic says FlashProve can verify LLM inference at 110 tokens per second on one H100, turning trust into infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI faces an internal espionage scare
items.oneliner: An OpenAI engineer was arrested after a hidden spy device was found onsite, reminding labs that frontier security is physical too.

items.title: A fake interview enabled a massive crypto theft
items.oneliner: North Korean operators allegedly used a fake job interview to help steal $6.3B from Binance, weaponizing hiring pipelines.

items.title: Debian patched a root-level apt flaw
items.oneliner: Debian fixed an apt redirect bug that let man-in-the-middle attackers potentially run malicious packages as root.

items.title: MCP OAuth setups still invite phishing
items.oneliner: Many MCP servers still accept arbitrary redirect URIs, which means user-controlled clients can quietly become OAuth phishing holes.

items.title: Linux loses badly on Nvidia AI laptops
items.oneliner: Encrypted Nvidia firmware can cut Linux inference speed to 35% on RTX Spark laptops, making Windows the practical ML stack.

items.title: Go finally replaced its aging JSON API
items.oneliner: Go 1.27 stabilizes encoding/json/v2 with stricter parsing and safer defaults, which should reduce silent bugs in production services.

items.title: Apple opened Siri AI to developers
items.oneliner: Apple opened Siri AI to all app developers, finally giving iOS builders a first-party path into voice-native agent workflows.
